body.spec:
The command `taskops studio` becomes `taskops ui`. Full spec:

1. `src/taskops/transports/cli/commands/studio.py` -> `ui.py` (git mv). The subparser registers as `ui` with help 'serve the live web interface (board, activity, reports)'. Register a SECOND hidden alias parser `studio` that runs the same `run` and prints ONE deprecation line to stderr: 'taskops studio is now taskops ui' before serving. Keep every flag identical (--host --port --token --readonly --rate-limit).
2. `git mv studio ui` at the repo root (the TS source dir). Update `ui/build.mjs` outdir comment if it names studio, `ui/package.json` name -> taskops-ui, and any path references: grep -r 'studio' across README.md, USAGE.md, CHANGELOG.md (add an Unreleased bullet), tests, pyproject (no change needed: bundle path transports/http/ui is ALREADY ui). The _MISSING page in transports/http/static.py says 'cd studio && npm install' -> 'cd ui && ...'.
3. `taskops ui` banner prints 'taskops ui -> http://...'.
4. Rebuild the bundle: cd ui && npm install && npm run build. Commit the regenerated bundle.

DONE = `taskops ui` serves, `taskops studio` still works with the deprecation line, gates green: `.venv/bin/python3 -m pytest` (all ~604 tests) and `ruff check .`. Update any test that invokes the studio command name. Do NOT touch the engine, http transport routes, or the MCP.
body.title: Rename studio -> taskops ui (command, dir, docs)

body.spec:
Reshape `taskops --help` from 19 commands to 7 visible: init, ui, tasks, report, run(later), recover, sync. Spec:

1. NEW command module `tasks.py`: `taskops tasks` with subcommands, EVERY one a thin wrapper over EXISTING usecases (no new logic):
   - `taskops tasks` (no sub) / `tasks list`: compact list one line per open task: mark id status title holder. Reuse usecases.board() and render a compact list (new small renderer render_tasklist in render/board.py or a new render/tasklist.py, pure).
   - `tasks show <id>` -> usecases.ask + render_view (what `ask <id>` does today)
   - `tasks add <title> [--spec S] [--after id,id] [--files f,g] [--priority N] [--label l]` -> usecases.plan with a one-entry list. Prints the id.
   - `tasks plan <file.json|->` -> existing plan command behaviour moved here
   - `tasks done <id> [-m comment] [--no-code]` -> usecases.update status=done
   - `tasks release <id> -m comment` -> usecases.update status=released
   - `tasks log <id>` -> usecases.session_log + render_log (today's `log` command)
   - `tasks search <text>` -> usecases.search + render_search
2. Grouping in main.py: keep ALL existing top-level commands working as aliases (next, update, ask, plan, dispatch, log, guard, ingest, brief, inbox, track, checkout, hook, studio-alias from the other card) but HIDE them from the help listing. argparse: register hidden commands with `help=argparse.SUPPRESS`. The visible set: init, ui, tasks, report, recover, sync (+ dispatch stays hidden; run comes in a later card).
3. Respect the architecture: transports may not import storage/engine (tests/architecture enforces). File budget: max 70 code lines per module — split tasks.py into tasks.py + _tasks_args.py if needed, following the existing command-module pattern (register(sub) + set_defaults(run=...)).
4. Tests: extend tests/transports (there is CLI coverage in e2e) with: `tasks add` creates a card and prints its id; `tasks done` refuses without commit (same guard message); hidden commands still execute; `--help` output does NOT contain 'guard' or 'brief'.

DONE = taskops --help shows only the 7-ish visible commands, every old invocation still works, all tests + ruff green. CHANGELOG Unreleased bullet explaining the regroup and why (three audiences were mixed).
body.title: Regroup the CLI: taskops tasks domain, hook group hidden, agent group

body.spec:
A new projection: everything that happened on ONE calendar day, hyper-detailed, derived from events.jsonl + git. NO storage, NO LLM. Spec:

1. Contract `DayReport` in contracts/board.py (or a new contracts/day.py): {repo, date str YYYY-MM-DD, closed: list[ClosedCard], in_flight: list[Task], blocked: list[Task], conversations: list[Event], actors: list[ActorRoll], commits_total: int}. ClosedCard = {task: Task, actor who closed, claimed_ts, done_ts, commits: list[CommitStat]}. CommitStat = CommitRef + {additions int, deletions int}.
2. Engine module engine/day.py: `day_report(store, date)` cuts the window at LOCAL calendar midnight [00:00, 24:00) of the given date. Reuse events.since + tasks_of + _rolls from engine/history.py (import _rolls or extract a shared helper — do NOT duplicate). Closed = events kind=done that day. In-flight = tasks touched that day still open. Conversations = comment/message events that day.
3. Commit stats: ONE batched subprocess, mirroring engine/gitstate.branch_states style: `git diff-tree --numstat -r <sha1> <sha2> ...` does not batch across commits, so use `git log --numstat --format=%H --no-walk <sha1> <sha2> ...` parsed into {sha: (adds, dels, files)}. Never raise: on any git failure return zeros (same degrade rule as gitio). Put it in engine/gitstate.py or a new engine/diffstat.py.
4. Render render/day.py (pure): the dossier as markdown — header line with counts, '## Cerrado' with per-card: mark, id, title, actor, claim->done duration, each commit as `sha subject (+adds -dels)` + first files, comment count and last comment text; '## En vuelo / bloqueado'; '## Conversaciones'; '## Por actor'. Match the existing render style (_text.py helpers, STATUS_MARK, ago).
5. CLI: `taskops report day [--date yesterday|YYYY-MM-DD]` (default today) in commands/report.py. Parse 'today'/'yesterday'/ISO date; refuse anything else with an actionable message (pattern: parse_window in usecases/report.py).
6. Usecase report.py: `day(start, date_text)` wrapper.
7. MCP: in contracts/tools.py ReportParams, kind Literal becomes ['board','standup','day'] — REMOVE 'fleet' and 'burndown'. Add optional `date` field with description in _fields.py. Update _reads.report_ to route 'day' and drop the fleet/burndown branches (keep usecases.fleet itself — the HTTP api still serves /api/fleet). Update _descriptions REPORT text.
8. Tests: tests/engine/test_day.py — a card claimed at 23:50 and closed at 00:10 lands on the CLOSING day; window cuts at midnight not rolling 24h; numstat parse from a fixture string; degrade to zeros without git. tests/transports: report day via CLI happy path; MCP report kind=day returns text; kind=fleet now REJECTED by schema/handler with a clear message.

DONE = `taskops report day --date yesterday` prints the dossier against a real repo, all tests + ruff + architecture invariants green (70 code lines/module budget!), CHANGELOG bullet.
body.title: report day: the deterministic daily dossier (engine + render + CLI + MCP enum)

body.spec:
Today a card's spec/title cannot change after creation — a real, documented gap. Spec:

1. New event kind 'edited' in _types.py EventKind + EVENT_KINDS, body {field: 'spec'|'title'|'priority', to: value, from: value}. One event per changed field.
2. Storage: TaskTable gains set_field(task_id, field, value, when) or reuse a generic update — SQL stays ONLY in storage/.
3. Usecase: extend usecases/update.py (or a small usecases/edit.py if the 70-line budget forces it) with edit(root, task_id, *, title=None, spec=None, priority=None, actor). Records one 'edited' event per change, bumps updated. Editing a done/cancelled card is REFUSED (BadRequest: 'closed cards are history — open a new card referencing it').
4. Replay: engine/replay.py adds 'edited' to REPLAYED and applies it with the same newer-wins rule as _status (event ts vs task.updated) so two machines converge.
5. CLI: `taskops tasks edit <id> [--title T] [--spec S] [--priority N]` in the tasks domain (this card DEPENDS on the CLI regroup card; if tasks.py is not merged yet, rebase on it). At least one flag required.
6. MCP: add optional title/spec/priority-edit? NO — keep the tool surface unchanged; editing is a human act, CLI+UI only. State this in the CHANGELOG bullet.
7. Tests: edit changes the row and writes the event; replaying the event on a fresh clone converges; editing a done card is refused; an older edited event does not clobber a newer local edit.

DONE = taskops tasks edit works end to end, sync between two stores converges (mirror the pattern of existing e2e sync tests), all gates green.
body.title: tasks edit: editar spec/title/priority de una card (evento edited + replay)

body.spec:
Persist the daily dossier as an immutable committed file, ready to carry an LLM narration. Spec:

1. `taskops report day --write` renders the layer-1 dossier (from the 'report day' card — this DEPENDS on it) and writes `.taskops/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. The file starts with an HTML comment fingerprint: `<!-- taskops:report date=2026-07-27 max_seq=812 generated=<iso> -->` where max_seq = store.events.max_seq() at generation time. If the file exists, REFUSE unless --force (a report someone may have cited must not silently change).
2. `.taskops/reports/` is COMMITTED (not gitignored): check usecases/setup.py gitignore block — it must ignore db.sqlite etc but NOT reports/. Adjust the block if needed and make init idempotent about it.
3. A section marker in the file: after the dossier, a line `## Narración` followed by `_pendiente — generala con /taskops:digest_`. The skill replaces that section.
4. Plugin skill `plugin/skills/digest/SKILL.md`: instructs the SESSION to (a) run `taskops report day --date $1 --write` if the file does not exist, (b) READ the .md dossier, (c) write a human narration — what mattered, decisions, risks, what needs a human — REPLACING the Narración section body, (d) never invent facts not in the dossier, (e) commit the file with message 'taskops: report YYYY-MM-DD'. Follow the tone rules of the existing standup skill (no flattery, lead with what needs a human).
5. HTTP: GET /api/report?date=YYYY-MM-DD returns {date, dossier_md, exists, stale: bool, missing_events: int} — stale = current max_seq for that day's window > fingerprint max_seq. Wire in router + api.py, guarded like the others.
6. Tests: --write writes fingerprint + refuses overwrite without --force; the api endpoint reports stale correctly after appending an event inside that day; init leaves reports/ tracked.

DONE = write, re-read, stale detection all tested; skill file present; gates green; CHANGELOG bullet.
body.title: report day --write + digest: reporte del dia persistido en .taskops/reports/

body.spec:
Expose the existing spawn path under an honest name. Spec:

1. New visible CLI command `taskops run [ids... | --count N] [--model M] [--dry-run]` = exactly usecases.dispatch(..., spawn=True). Before spawning (not on --dry-run), print to stderr: '⚠ each worker is a NEW billed Claude session — for free parallelism dispatch sub-agents from a session (taskops_dispatch)' and require confirmation unless --yes. Reuse render_dispatch.
2. `taskops dispatch` (the old command) stays as a hidden alias; its --spawn flag now says 'deprecated: use taskops run'.
3. The MCP surface does NOT change — no spawn from a model, the DispatchParams docstring already explains why. Do not touch it.
4. Tests: run --dry-run prints the would-dispatch table and starts nothing; run --yes with a stubbed spawn (monkeypatch engine spawn like existing dispatch tests do) launches; confirmation refusal aborts cleanly.
5. Help text marks it: 'run cards with headless Claude workers (experimental, billed)'.

DONE = taskops run visible in help next to the other 6, old dispatch behaviour intact, gates green, CHANGELOG bullet.

ui: the read-only and token refusals name the command that prints the URL

body.text: Renamed taskops studio -> taskops ui. (1) git mv studio/ -> ui/ and commands/studio.py -> ui.py; the subparser registers as `ui` with help "serve the live web interface (board, activity, reports)", and a second parser `studio` registered WITHOUT help (hidden from --help) shares one _flags() helper so the alias cannot drift, sets deprecated_name=True, and run() prints "taskops studio is now taskops ui" to stderr before serving. Banner now reads "taskops ui -> http://...". (2) ui/package.json + lock name -> taskops-ui, build.mjs log "ui built ->", index.html title, static.py _MISSING page now says "ui not built" / "cd ui && npm install && npm run build". (3) Docs: USAGE.md (all invocations, env table, troubleshooting, the Changing the UI block, plus a note that the old name still works), README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, CHANGELOG.md Unreleased bullet, docs/guia.html + docs/flujos.html (ASCII diagram padding re-aligned), .gitignore ui/node_modules, pyproject comment. (4) HTTP policy refusals now say "this board is read-only" and "open the URL `taskops ui` printed". (5) New tests/transports/test_cli.py: 4 tests pinning that `ui` exists, `studio` still parses and marks itself deprecated, the alias takes EXACTLY the same flags as ui, and `studio` is absent from --help. (6) Rebuilt the bundle (npm install && npm run build) and committed it; npm run check reports no drift. GATES: pytest 608 passed (604 before + my 4), ruff check . All checks passed. Smoke: both `taskops studio` and `taskops ui` serve HTTP 200, and the alias prints the single deprecation line first. Commits 276bbbe, 2442773 on tk/tk-dc436a/rename-studio-taskops-ui-command. body.subject: report day: one calendar day in full, with each commit's diff size

body.text: report day shipped: contracts/day.py (DayReport/ClosedCard/CommitStat), engine/day.py (local-midnight window via mktime, so a DST day is 23 or 25h and never start+86400), engine/_closed.py (per-card assembly), engine/diffstat.py (ONE batched `git log --numstat --format=%H --no-walk`; diff-tree cannot batch — it diffs the first sha against the rest — and it degrades to {} like the rest of gitio), render/day.py + render/_dossier.py (pure), CLI `taskops report day [--date today|yesterday|YYYY-MM-DD]`, usecase day()/parse_date(). Reused instead of duplicating: history._rolls became public history.rolls (one roll-up, two projections), _types.WORKING_STATUSES for in flight, and _text.ago is now written in terms of a new _text.span so a duration and a distance-from-now round the same way. MCP: ReportParams.kind is now board|standup|day, fleet and burndown REMOVED and an unknown kind is refused rather than falling through to the board (usecases.fleet and the HTTP /api/fleet untouched); new `date` field + REPORT_KIND/REPORT description rewritten. Heartbeat (activity) events are excluded from the dossier. Tests: tests/engine/test_day.py (12 — midnight cut vs rolling 24h, an event exactly at 00:00 is inside, a card claimed 23:50 and closed 00:10 files under the CLOSING day, numstat parse incl. binary `-` and empty commits, zeros without git) and tests/transports/test_day_report.py (7 — CLI happy path, bad date refused, MCP day returns text, enum is exactly the three kinds, fleet/burndown now error). GATES GREEN from the worktree: pytest 653 passed, ruff clean, and also mypy + pyright clean. NOTE for whoever runs the gates next: the venv has taskops installed editable from /Users/berna/taskops/src, so a bare `pytest` in a worktree tests MAIN, not your branch — run it with PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src. Docs synced: CHANGELOG (two bullets), README (tool table + the burndown paragraph), USAGE (1.7 + CLI reference), docs/guia+flujos.html, and the two plugin skills that told agents to call `taskops_report fleet` — which would now be refused. Did not touch studio/ or the studio command (v21 is renaming it). Commit 931a00a.

body.text: Regrouped the CLI: new `taskops tasks` domain (list/show/add/plan/done/release/log/search), each subcommand a wrapper over an existing run — tasks show/search ARE ask.run, done/release ARE update.run with the status preset — so no logic is duplicated and the commit guard cannot be bypassed through the new door. --help now lists init, ui, tasks, report, recover, sync; the agent verbs and hook plumbing register through an _Unlisted proxy that drops `help`, so they parse and run exactly as before. New pure renderer render/tasklist.py. --repo/--actor inherit via argparse.SUPPRESS so both flag orders work. 8 new tests in tests/transports/test_cli.py. Gates green: pytest all passed, ruff clean.
